objects.name: Chipkin Example B-SCHUB
objects.note: vendor 389 (Chipkin Automation Systems); the series' device instance for B-SCHUB; instance configurable with --deviceID and name with --device-name. The stack rows are device-wide facts only the stack knows - the protocol version and revision it implements, the services and object types it was configured with, the live object list and address-binding table. The accepted rows are the stack's configured defaults for APDU limits, segmentation, system status and database revision; an application that answered them from its own constants could contradict the stack, so the example does not. Segmentation_Supported is segmented-both, the CAS BACnet Stack's segmentation configuration (6.x default, cas-bacnet-stack#2992); with it the stack also serves Max_Segments_Accepted (16) and APDU_Segment_Timeout (5000 ms) - see section 5

objects.name: Bronze
objects.note: REAL, degrees Celsius; starts at 21.5; read-only (a sample value, changed with the arrow keys)

objects.name: BACnet IP
objects.note: BACnet/IP; present only when the example is started with --port <n> (BACnet/SC is the only data link otherwise). Network_Type and Protocol_Level are set from BACnetStack_AddNetworkPortObject()'s arguments (IPv4, BACnet Application) at start-up, not a GetProperty callback like the object's other app-served rows; Changes_Pending is likewise computed and answered natively by the stack's Network Port object. IP_Address and IP_Subnet_Mask are read from the computer's primary interface at start-up, IP_Default_Gateway is 0.0.0.0, BACnet_IP_UDP_Port is the --port value. Reliability has no fault condition this example detects, so it is accepted at the generic default (normal). Network_Number is 0 with Network_Number_Quality unknown unless --ip-network-number sets it (then quality configured); the device is not a router. Command (cl. 12.56.16) is present and writable, executed by the stack (DISCARD_CHANGES reverts the port's pending changes)

objects.name: BACnet SC
objects.note: BACnet/SC (Network_Type = secureConnect(11)); the device's only Network Port unless the example is started with --port (then Network Port 1 is the BACnet/IP port). Hosts the NM-SCH-B hub function (listener, at most 4 devices) and, with --sc-hub-uri, the hub connector; the WebSocket/TLS transport is sc_transport/ScTransport. Network_Type and Protocol_Level are set from BACnetStack_AddNetworkPortObject()'s arguments at start-up, not a GetProperty callback like the object's other app-served rows; Changes_Pending is likewise computed and answered natively by the stack's Network Port object. Reliability has no fault condition the hub detects, so it is accepted at the generic default (normal). Network_Number is 0 with Network_Number_Quality unknown unless --sc-network-number sets it (then quality configured); the device is not a router. Command (cl. 12.56.16) is writable: DISCARD_CHANGES also drops staged certificate writes, and GENERATE_CSR_FILE makes a new key pair and Certificate Signing Request (File 2) - the NetworkPortCommand callback in main.cpp

objects.name: Operational Certificate
objects.note: writable over BACnet (clause 19.8.3): File_Size and AtomicWriteFile, staged until ReinitializeDevice ACTIVATE_CHANGES/WARMSTART, which validates the set (parses, matches the hub's private key, chains to an issuer) before writing opr-hub.pem and reloading TLS. Serves the hub's operational certificate via AtomicReadFile (stream access) - bound to Network Port 2's Operational_Certificate_File. File_Size/Modification_Date come from the staged copy or the file on disk

objects.name: Certificate Signing Request
objects.note: read-only; serves the hub's certificate signing request (CARI cert1/device-<n>/port-2/csr-hub.pem) - bound to Network Port 2's Certificate_Signing_Request_File. rewritten by the hub on Network Port 2 Command GENERATE_CSR_FILE, for a new key that replaces the hub's key when a certificate signed for it is activated

objects.name: Issuer Certificate Slot 1
objects.note: writable over BACnet (clause 19.8.3), same staging as File 1; issuer certificate slot 1 (CARI cert1/issuer/iss-1.pem) - one of Network Port 2's 2 Issuer_Certificate_Files entries

objects.name: Issuer Certificate Slot 2
objects.note: writable over BACnet (clause 19.8.3), same staging as File 1; issuer certificate slot 2 (CARI cert1/issuer/iss-2.pem once written; until then it serves slot 1's certificate). TLS trusts every issuer in both slots (trusted-issuers.pem)
